alt.en: A printed book page numbered 256 and headed "Scottish Songs", with the title "Annie Laurie", two eight-line verses beginning "Maxwelltown banks are bonnie" and "She's backet like a peacock", and below them the start of a prose note beginning "I found this song in the little Ballad Book".
alt.es: Página impresa de un libro, con el número 256 y el encabezado "Scottish Songs", con el título "Annie Laurie", dos estrofas de ocho versos que empiezan "Maxwelltown banks are bonnie" y "She's backet like a peacock", y debajo el comienzo de una nota en prosa que empieza "I found this song in the little Ballad Book".

caption.en: The old two-verse song as the poet Allan Cunningham reprinted it from Sharpe's Ballad Book in his Songs of Scotland (London, 1825), peacock verse and all; Lady John Scott found the words in a book of Cunningham's and rewrote that verse.
caption.es: La antigua canción de dos estrofas tal como el poeta Allan Cunningham la reimprimió, tomada del Ballad Book de Sharpe, en sus Songs of Scotland (Londres, 1825), con la estrofa del pavo real; Lady John Scott encontró la letra en un libro de Cunningham y rehízo esa estrofa.

source: Allan Cunningham, The Songs of Scotland, Ancient and Modern, vol. 3 (London: John Taylor, 1825), p. 256, "Annie Laurie"
library: University of California Libraries (UCLA; digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed London 1825; Allan Cunningham died 1842, Sharpe (quoted) 1851. Internet Archive record: possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of California Libraries, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A printed page of music numbered 25 and headed "Annie Laurie", with the end of the song for voice and piano over the words "bonnie Annie Laurie, I'd lay me down and dee", two more verses in two columns beginning "Her brow is like the snaw-drift" and "Like dew on the gowan lying", and a long note in small type below a rule.
alt.es: Página de música impresa, con el número 25 y el encabezado "Annie Laurie", con el final de la canción para voz y piano sobre la letra "bonnie Annie Laurie, I'd lay me down and dee", dos estrofas más en dos columnas que empiezan "Her brow is like the snaw-drift" y "Like dew on the gowan lying", y una larga nota en letra pequeña bajo una raya.

caption.en: Annie Laurie in Graham's Songs of Scotland (Edinburgh, late 1840s), arranged by T. M. Mudie; the note below calls the air "quite modern" and gives its composer only as "Lady J" and "S" and "t", the rest printed as dashes.
caption.es: Annie Laurie en las Songs of Scotland de Graham (Edimburgo, finales de la década de 1840), con arreglo de T. M. Mudie; la nota de abajo llama a la melodía "bastante moderna" y nombra a su compositora solo con las letras "Lady J", "S" y "t": el resto se imprimió con rayas.

source: George Farquhar Graham, editor, The Songs of Scotland, Adapted to Their Appropriate Melodies, vol. 3 (Edinburgh: Wood and Co., undated; its notes quote a letter of 13 June 1849), p. 25, "Annie Laurie", arranged by T. M. Mudie, and note
library: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Printed Edinburgh, undated, not before mid-1849 (vol. 3 quotes a letter of 13 June 1849); editor G. F. Graham died 1867, arranger T. M. Mudie 1876, Lady John Scott (words) 1900, Robert Chambers (quoted) 1871. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of Toronto, Faculty of Music Library, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: A foxed, stained page of engraved music numbered 2, headed "Annie Laurie.", marked Moderato, with a piano introduction and then voice and piano over the words "Maxwelton braes are bonnie, Where early fa's the dew; And its there that Annie Laurie, Gie'd me her promise true", and the plate number 793 at the foot.
alt.es: Página de música grabada, con manchas y moteado, con el número 2 y el encabezado "Annie Laurie.", marcada Moderato, con una introducción de piano y luego voz y piano sobre la letra "Maxwelton braes are bonnie, Where early fa's the dew; And its there that Annie Laurie, Gie'd me her promise true", y el número de plancha 793 al pie.

caption.en: The first page of the New York sheet our arrangement is read from (William Hall & Son, plate 793, about 1850), marked Moderato, with no composer or poet named.
caption.es: La primera página de la partitura de Nueva York de la que está tomado nuestro arreglo (William Hall & Son, plancha 793, hacia 1850), marcada Moderato, sin nombre de compositor ni de poeta.

source: Annie Laurie (New York: William Hall & Son, 239 Broadway; catalogued 1848, the Jenny Lind cover points to 1850 or later), plate 793, p. 2
library: Washington University in St. Louis, Gaylord Music Library (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Published New York about 1848 to 1858, unsigned; Lady John Scott (words and tune) died 1900.
